requirements.question: **★** What should the product be called (working name, final name, branding/domain)?
requirements.acceptance: Show ChunkMaestro and MrFrydae consistently in product metadata; reject remaining CraftHelm branding.

requirements.question: **★** Private personal tool, a shareable self-hosted app, an open-source community product, or commercial SaaS?
requirements.acceptance: Describe distribution as source-available; fail release review if commercial restrictions are called OSI open source.

requirements.question: **★** GitHub repo name/owner, public vs private, and preferred license (MIT, Apache-2.0, AGPL-3.0, proprietary, undecided)?
requirements.acceptance: With no approved license, stable publication is blocked and no LICENSE is generated; record owner-selected competition terms before unblocking.

requirements.question: **★** Which features must be in an initial usable v0.1 versus a polished v1.0?
requirements.acceptance: Account for every selected feature by v1.0 except Apex; detect any silently deferred selected requirement in milestone review.

requirements.question: Are you the only administrator, or will friends/moderators have separate accounts and granular permissions?
requirements.acceptance: Initialize one local owner and enforce core permission checks; absence of moderator accounts must not bypass authorization.

requirements.question: Do you foresee supporting more than one Minecraft network/household/account at once?
requirements.acceptance: Create two networks with different credential scopes; a credential granted to one cannot mutate the other.

requirements.question: Expected maximum number of hosts, servers, concurrent online players and worlds (today / 1 year / 3 years)?
requirements.acceptance: Benchmark approximately 20 instances with hardware and workload recorded; leave unmeasured player/world limits unspecified.

requirements.question: Should the app manage only Minecraft Java/Bedrock proxies, or eventually other games/processes?
requirements.acceptance: Represent Java and Geyser Bedrock connectivity; offer no other-game or native Bedrock process provisioning capability.

requirements.question: Do you want the panel to create and initialize brand-new Minecraft servers or only adopt existing ones?
requirements.acceptance: Adopt an existing instance and provision a reviewed new template; reject arbitrary bootstrap commands.

requirements.question: Should the product work fully without any cloud account, license server, telemetry or external database?
requirements.acceptance: Disconnect internet and open local state/staging without cloud login; no telemetry or license-server dependency is contacted.

requirements.question: **★** What is the host OS and version of your current Minecraft VM (Debian, Ubuntu, etc.)?
requirements.acceptance: Display recorded Debian host facts as point-in-time inventory; require fresh inspection before mutating runtime based on them.

requirements.question: **★** What is its `systemd` unit name and service user (no secrets needed)?
requirements.acceptance: Manually adopt the recorded minecraft.service mapping after verification; reject a mismatched service user.

requirements.question: **★** What are the Minecraft working directory, plugin directory, server JAR path, Java version, and launch method?
requirements.acceptance: Inspect configured root/JAR/launcher/Java before changes; preserve existing launch settings when compatibility is unverified.

requirements.question: **★** Where should the main control-plane backend run: desktop machine, existing Linux VM, new VM, Docker host, or selectable install modes?
requirements.acceptance: Migrate database, credential references, trust and backup access to a second desktop; the old desktop cannot issue writes afterward.

requirements.question: Which virtualizers are relevant: Proxmox, XCP-ng, VMware, Hyper-V, another, or none?
requirements.acceptance: Select an XCP-ng adapter for optional hypervisor operations; absent credentials show unavailable rather than invented VM state.

requirements.question: Are VMs all on one trusted LAN, across VLANs, VPNs, remote sites, or public hosting?
requirements.acceptance: Connect an enrolled host over approved LAN/VPN; an unapproved network cannot reach an automatically public listener.

requirements.question: **★** How should remote host connectivity work: installed agent dialing out, SSH with keys, direct HTTPS/mTLS, WireGuard/Tailscale, or multiple modes?
requirements.acceptance: Install using SSH keys then establish outbound agent mTLS; desktop disconnect leaves an approved local occurrence executable.

requirements.question: Do you want an agentless SSH fallback for one-off or legacy machines?
requirements.acceptance: Register an SSH-only host and inspect supported operations; autonomous ChunkMaestro schedules are unavailable without the agent.

requirements.question: Should enrollment use a temporary pairing code, QR code, signed provisioning file, command copied from UI, or all?
requirements.acceptance: Copy an enrollment command with expiring single-use token; replay or expiration fails and no permanent key appears in the command.

requirements.question: Can the host agent run as a restricted service account with preapproved service-specific `sudoers` rules, or will you explicitly permit elevated functionality?
requirements.acceptance: Run agent and Minecraft under distinct restricted identities; arbitrary sudo, shell and protected-file writes are denied.

requirements.question: Can one VM host more than one Minecraft instance (`systemd` units, Docker containers, or both)?
requirements.acceptance: Register two native instances on one VM with separate TCP/UDP reservations; conflicting endpoints are rejected.

requirements.question: Should the panel discover Minecraft instances automatically, prompt before adopting them, or require manual registration?
requirements.acceptance: Discover a running process without adopting it; only explicit manual registration creates ownership.

requirements.question: Is Docker/Podman Minecraft management an initial requirement or a later provider adapter?
requirements.acceptance: Native setup requires no Docker/Podman; advertise no container operations until a separately approved adapter exists.

requirements.question: Should hypervisor integration display VM power, snapshots, CPU/memory/disk and optionally create/restart VMs?
requirements.acceptance: Read XCP-ng power/snapshots/resources and review a VM lifecycle proposal; Minecraft restart permission cannot power off the VM.

requirements.question: How should offline hosts behave in the UI—last-known state, queue operations for later, or reject changes until online?
requirements.acceptance: Drop connection after a restart was submitted: show stale state and unknown outcome, reject new interactive work, reconcile journal without replay; a missed host occurrence stays missed.

requirements.question: **★** Which server software must be supported at launch: Paper, Purpur, Spigot, Vanilla, Folia, Fabric, Forge, NeoForge, Velocity, BungeeCord?
requirements.acceptance: Evaluate Paper, Spigot, Vanilla, Folia, Fabric, Velocity and BungeeCord fixtures separately; unsupported rich capabilities stay disabled.

requirements.question: **★** Which Minecraft version(s) are you running and which version families must be supported (current only, N-2, broad legacy)?
requirements.acceptance: Require a pinned N-2 family policy and independent MC/Java/Bedrock/bridge compatibility rows; reject an unverified version combination.

requirements.question: **★** Do you already use RCON; should the app use it, avoid it, or use it only when a bridge/agent is not installed?
requirements.acceptance: Use authorized private/local RCON for a game command; RCON credentials never authorize host-shell execution.

requirements.question: Should the app install a small optional Paper/Spigot plugin for rich stats, plugin state, player actions and Multiverse integration?
requirements.acceptance: Install a compatible optional bridge after detection; reject the bridge on an unsupported server API.

requirements.question: Should JVM flags, Java runtime versions, RAM allocation, environment variables and unit overrides be editable from the UI?
requirements.acceptance: Preview allowed heap/Java edits and restart need; reject arbitrary environment, executable and JVM argument fields.

requirements.question: Should an agent be permitted to edit the systemd service file itself or only selected configuration fields after explicit confirmation?
requirements.acceptance: Apply an approved typed setting through the root-owned helper; direct agent writes to units/launchers and arbitrary service templates fail.

requirements.question: Should start/stop/restart support warning broadcasts, countdowns, player-drain and maintenance-mode gates?
requirements.acceptance: Advance a real five-minute warning, kick remaining players, save, gracefully stop then start; online players do not cause indefinite postponement.

requirements.question: Should server startup include automated health checks, log-signature detection and crash-loop protection?
requirements.acceptance: Inject a startup failure and repeated crashes; expose uncertain health and enforce crash-loop protection without retrying a failed deploy.

requirements.question: Should Minecraft core updates and Java runtime updates be manually initiated, scheduled with approval, or optionally automatic?
requirements.acceptance: Stage core/Java updates for next approved service restart; no VM reboot or unattended installation occurs absent approved policy.

requirements.question: Should new servers be provisioned from templates and allocated unused TCP/UDP ports with port-conflict checks?
requirements.acceptance: Preview a reviewed template with unused TCP/UDP ports; collision or unapproved unit/path prevents provisioning.

requirements.question: Should the app inspect logs for probable crashes and propose troubleshooting steps, or only show raw logs and links?
requirements.acceptance: Match a known crash signature and show raw evidence with a suggestion; suggestion alone never changes host files.

requirements.question: Should server configuration be tracked as a desired state with drift detection versus only on-demand edits?
requirements.acceptance: Change a selected host setting manually: show drift and Apply/Adopt choice; do not reconcile worlds, logs, caches or binaries automatically.

requirements.question: **★** Are you running an existing proxy (Waterfall/BungeeCord/Velocity), planning one, or starting with independent servers?
requirements.acceptance: Show Velocity as planned and current proxy as unverified; do not show an installed proxy without observation.

requirements.question: **★** Are you willing to standardize new networks on Velocity while retaining legacy compatibility?
requirements.acceptance: Default a new network to Velocity while exposing separately tested BungeeCord compatibility; unsupported legacy actions stay unavailable.

requirements.question: Should the app install/manage the proxy process, or only edit and monitor an existing proxy?
requirements.acceptance: Review proxy lifecycle/configuration and installation plans; no Traefik or HAProxy control is offered.

requirements.question: Should the network topology be an editable drag-and-drop graph, a generated diagram, a tree, or several views?
requirements.acceptance: Open graph, searchable table and inspector; dragging a node changes layout without changing routing configuration.

requirements.question: Should the panel configure routing (lobby/fallback/priority), backend server lists, health checks and secure player forwarding?
requirements.acceptance: Review supported backend/fallback/forwarding changes; invalid fields or unprotected forwarding secrets prevent apply.

requirements.question: Should backend additions/removals automatically propose proxy config changes with a review and maintenance window?
requirements.acceptance: Add a backend and observe a proposed proxy diff with affected players/window; no live configuration changes before approval.

requirements.question: Do you need network-level chat, proxy-wide player list, cross-server teleport/transfer, network bans or shared inventory hooks?
requirements.acceptance: Provide capability-gated network list/transfer; chat, shared inventories and network bans remain unavailable until exact integrations and semantics are approved.

requirements.question: **★** Is Geyser/Floodgate already in use; should Bedrock players and endpoints be first-class in v0.1?
requirements.acceptance: Represent Java TCP and Bedrock UDP separately with health/edition; absent Geyser detection never enables dependent controls.

requirements.question: Should network health include UDP probes, external connect checks, compatibility alerts and firewall troubleshooting?
requirements.acceptance: Fail UDP while TCP succeeds and report separate observations with vantage/time; firewall fixes remain proposals until authorized.

requirements.question: **★** Are you using Multiverse-Core today? Which version and addons (Portals, Inventories, NetherPortals, etc.)?
requirements.acceptance: Detect Multiverse core/addon versions; absent or unverified addons disable their controls.

requirements.question: Which Multiverse operations matter most: list worlds, create, clone, import, load/unload, rename, delete, teleport, gamerules, spawn, portals?
requirements.acceptance: Exercise version-supported world listing/properties, load/unload, teleport, spawn, gamerules, create/import/clone; rename/delete require verified recovery point, stronger confirmation and version checks; absent integration denies controls.

requirements.question: Do you want a visual world graph/cards, or a compact searchable table with detailed inspector?
requirements.acceptance: Search worlds in table/inspector and optional cards; relationship edges appear only from detected reliable link data.

requirements.question: Should worlds have independent resource/disk/backup policies and individual role permissions?
requirements.acceptance: Apply per-world retention/disk/permission policy; never present independent per-world CPU/RAM enforcement.

requirements.question: Do you need cross-server world-copy/import workflows? Should such operations require a scheduled stop or freeze?
requirements.acceptance: Copy a consistent recovery point to a stopped destination after capacity/version checks; reject unguarded live copy and provide reviewed recovery.

requirements.question: **★** Where is your preferred staging directory physically located: your Mac/Windows desktop, the backend VM, a NAS share, a Git checkout, or configurable per machine?
requirements.acceptance: Choose desktop-local or optional NAS staging per server; reject storing the active SQLite database in shared staging.

requirements.question: **★** Should staging sync be one-way staging → server, bidirectional with conflicts, or selectable per folder?
requirements.acceptance: Deploy local changes one way and require explicit Import from server; no background bidirectional overwrite occurs.

requirements.question: Should the desktop monitor staging changes continuously (filesystem watcher) or refresh on demand?
requirements.acceptance: Modify a staged file and observe watcher refresh; watcher failure is surfaced and never triggers deployment.

requirements.question: Should any changed local file deploy automatically, or always require a reviewed plan and approval?
requirements.acceptance: Change a local file and inspect a plan awaiting approval; remote bytes remain unchanged until approval.

requirements.question: **★** Is a required restart after plugin JAR changes acceptable, with only verified plugin-specific commands offered as optional reloads?
requirements.acceptance: Replace a plugin JAR and require restart; offer reload only for exact documented plugin/version with approval.

requirements.question: Should each server have independent staging profiles, shared templates, and environment overlays (`dev`, `test`, `production`)?
requirements.acceptance: Combine shared defaults and production overlay with server override; preview resolves exact inherited values before apply.

requirements.question: Should files be assigned to multiple servers at once, with per-target previews and rollback?
requirements.acceptance: Target two servers and fail one: show separate previews/results/recovery points without claiming atomic fleet success.

requirements.question: What should happen when the server-side file changed after the last sync: stop, prompt diff/merge, prefer local, prefer remote?
requirements.acceptance: Alter remote file after sync and attempt deployment; block that file and require explicit diff/merge or winner choice.

requirements.question: Should the staging UI be two-pane file trees, three-pane with a deployment basket, or Git-style changed-file list?
requirements.acceptance: Navigate local/server trees, add changes to third-pane basket and view a diff; removing a basket entry leaves it unapplied.

requirements.question: What editing modes do you want: raw editor, validated form, side-by-side YAML/JSON/properties, visual diff/merge, all?
requirements.acceptance: Edit supported config raw/form and compare side-by-side; preserve supported formatting/comments or warn before lossy save.

requirements.question: Should drag-and-drop uploads, folder import, copy/paste, create/delete/rename/move and archive extraction be supported?
requirements.acceptance: Import/move/extract into staging with content preview; reject traversal, escaping symlinks and archive bombs before writes escape root.

requirements.question: Should the app create Git commits and tags for each staged deployment, or use a built-in version history only?
requirements.acceptance: Record deployment in built-in history with Git disabled; optional Git export excludes secrets, worlds, logs and binaries by default.

requirements.question: Should deployment support scheduled maintenance windows, preflight scripts and post-deploy smoke tests?
requirements.acceptance: Run disk/port/version/backup/health checks for scheduled maintenance; failing check blocks apply and arbitrary shell hooks stay disabled.

requirements.question: Should failed health checks automatically roll back files and restart the server, or pause for confirmation?
requirements.acceptance: Fail post-deploy health and observe paused recovery choices; no automatic rollback/restart executes.

requirements.question: What backup threshold should be required before deployment: always, only risky changes, configurable, or manual?
requirements.acceptance: Attempt destructive/update/plugin/world mutation without verified recovery point and reject it; low-risk configurable policy is explicit.

requirements.question: Should deployments support draft, queued, approval-needed, in-progress, verifying, completed, failed and rolled-back statuses?
requirements.acceptance: Exercise draft/approval/scheduled/running/verifying/completed/failed/unknown/rolled-back transitions; offline interactive submission is rejected and approved scheduled results reconcile durably.

requirements.question: Do you want a shareable deployment manifest and reproducible release bundle for moving a server between hosts?
requirements.acceptance: Export versions/config/checksums/restoration instructions; replace secrets with references and flag redistribution restrictions.

requirements.question: Should the panel browse/install plugins from Hangar and Modrinth, with CurseForge or other sources later?
requirements.acceptance: Import from documented Hangar/Modrinth fixtures or manual JAR into staging; nothing installs live without reviewed deployment.

requirements.question: Should installed plugin metadata, dependencies, version compatibility, signatures/checksums and release notes be visible?
requirements.acceptance: Show installed/latest source/dependencies/license/checksum/release notes; unsigned checksum-only artifact is never labeled signature-verified.

requirements.question: Should it detect plugin JARs on disk that are not actually loaded, and failed/disabled plugins at runtime?
requirements.acceptance: Compare on-disk JAR and runtime report; distinguish installed/loaded/disabled/failed/unknown rather than infer loaded from disk.

requirements.question: What config formats must have rich editors (YAML, JSON/JSON5, TOML, `.properties`, XML, HOCON, INI)?
requirements.acceptance: Validate YAML, JSON/JSON5, TOML and properties fixtures; unsupported text retains raw editor without invented schema validation.

requirements.question: Would you like custom forms for known plugins (e.g., Geyser/Floodgate/Multiverse/LuckPerms) rather than raw file editing only?
requirements.acceptance: Detect supported Geyser/Floodgate/Multiverse/LuckPerms versions before showing typed forms; unsupported versions retain raw editing.

requirements.question: Should the panel identify whether a plugin supports a documented live config-reload command and invoke it only with your approval?
requirements.acceptance: Offer exact supported live reload with approval; deny global reload or unsupported plugin/version reload.

requirements.question: Should a plugin profile/template be reusable across every server in one network?
requirements.acceptance: Reuse a network plugin template with one server override; preview every target and never auto-deploy profile changes.

requirements.question: Do you need a plugin dependency graph, incompatible-version warnings and per-server staged updates?
requirements.acceptance: Stage incompatible/missing plugin dependencies and show graph/conflicts; uncertain compatibility remains unverified and blocks unsafe promotion.

requirements.question: Should the app edit `server.properties`, `paper-global.yml`, `paper-world-defaults.yml`, `spigot.yml`, `bukkit.yml` and JVM settings through typed forms?
requirements.acceptance: Round-trip versioned server/Paper/Spigot/Bukkit settings; privileged JVM fields outside helper allowlist are rejected.

requirements.question: Do you want per-field descriptions, inline documentation, dangerous-setting warnings and schema validation for common options?
requirements.acceptance: Show descriptions/defaults/restart needs and dangerous-setting warning; invalid field prevents approval.

requirements.question: Should the app create and edit datapacks/resource-pack configuration and upload world templates?
requirements.acceptance: Stage datapack/resource-pack/world-template import with compatibility and recovery checks; unsafe archive never reaches live root.

requirements.question: Do you want a pluggable plugin-specific UI/extension SDK for third-party authors later?
requirements.acceptance: Run sample versioned extension declaring grants; deny missing permissions and never load executable extension in privileged core/helper.

requirements.question: **★** Which metrics are non-negotiable on the landing page: online, uptime, TPS, MSPT, CPU, RAM, heap, disk, players, ping, network bytes, errors?
requirements.acceptance: Show status/uptime/players/CPU/RAM/heap/disk/latency/alerts and capability-gated TPS/MSPT; unsupported metric reads unavailable rather than zero.

requirements.question: How frequently should metrics update (1s, 2s, 5s, 10s, configurable), and how much historical detail do you want?
requirements.acceptance: Observe default five-second visible sampling and live console; hidden views reduce polling and user interval persists.

requirements.question: How long should SQLite retain raw/aggregated telemetry (24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, custom)?
requirements.acceptance: Advance fixture clock past 24h/30d/one year and verify raw/minute/hourly retention respectively; enforce configurable storage cap.

requirements.question: Should the app integrate with existing Prometheus/Grafana/Loki systems when available, or remain self-contained first?
requirements.acceptance: Operate dashboards without Prometheus/Grafana/Loki; optional integration failure cannot disable self-contained management.

requirements.question: Do you want per-world/per-chunk/entity statistics, JVM GC charts and flamegraphs using spark where supported?
requirements.acceptance: Initiate supported world/chunk/entity statistics, JVM GC views and spark flamegraph profiling with overhead notice and explicit time limit; unsupported sources show unavailable and profiling stops on expiry.

requirements.question: Should the metrics view compare servers side by side, include alerts and show timeline annotations for deployments/restarts?
requirements.acceptance: Compare two servers with deployment/restart/incident annotations and alerts; missing samples remain gaps with provenance.

requirements.question: Should the console support search, color/ANSI display, multi-server tabs, command completion, safe macros, and downloadable logs?
requirements.acceptance: Search/export redacted logs across tabs with sanitized ANSI and supported completion/macros; game commands cannot execute host shell.

requirements.question: Should commands entered in the panel be visible to all admins, only the author, or optionally masked for privacy?
requirements.acceptance: Record command author/outcome visible only to authorized server operators; recognized secrets and sensitive arguments are not retained.

requirements.question: **★** Which player actions must work: list, kick, ban, pardon, whitelist, op/deop, teleport, message, inventory, permission group?
requirements.acceptance: Exercise supported kick/ban/pardon/whitelist/message/transfer/groups; op/deop and inventory mutation require stronger confirmation and permissions.

requirements.question: Should player cards show names, avatars/skins, ping, playtime, session history, server, dimension/world and last seen?
requirements.acceptance: Render authoritative UUID/edition/world/session and optional avatar/playtime; missing fields show unavailable rather than fabricated values.

requirements.question: Should Bedrock/Floodgate identities be visibly distinguished and safely normalized with Java UUID handling?
requirements.acceptance: Create equal display names for Java and Floodgate players; authoritative edition/ID keeps records distinct.

requirements.question: Which alerts should exist: host offline, crash/restart loop, high MSPT, low TPS, low disk, failed backup, failed deployment, abnormal players, plugin errors?
requirements.acceptance: Inject offline/crash/poor performance/low disk/backup/deploy/plugin failures; deduplicate and cooldown notifications and leave unusual-player alerts opt-in.

requirements.question: Delivery methods: desktop push, in-app inbox, email, Discord webhook, Slack, Telegram, SMS, mobile push?
requirements.acceptance: Deliver inbox/desktop alerts offline; email/Discord send only after opt-in and provider failure preserves local inbox.

requirements.question: **★** Backup targets: same VM, separate NAS/NFS/SMB, S3-compatible object storage, external cloud provider, or multiple?
requirements.acceptance: With desktop off, run approved backup to configured NAS or bounded local store; incomplete transfer cannot claim off-host protection and local-only warns of VM-loss risk.

requirements.question: Do you want full snapshots, per-world backups, config/plugin-only backups and selective file restore?
requirements.acceptance: Create full/world/config-plugin recovery sets and selective restore; reject live world copy without supported consistency guard or stop.

requirements.question: Default frequency and retention (e.g., hourly 24, daily 14, weekly 8), storage quota and compression level?
requirements.acceptance: Keep daily 14-day and weekly eight-week backups plus required recovery points; enforce quota without pruning pinned risky-operation recovery.

requirements.question: Should backups be triggered before any restart, before deploy only, on fixed schedules, or manual?
requirements.acceptance: Run manual/approved local schedule and risky-change backups with desktop off; ordinary restart alone requires no new backup and destination failure is explicit.

requirements.question: Should the app verify restore integrity automatically by extracting into a sandbox and checking manifests?
requirements.acceptance: Extract recovery set in isolation and validate manifest/hash/readability; integrity-only success is not labeled successful server boot.

requirements.question: Should a failed deployment automatically restore backups, only restore staged config, or await owner confirmation?
requirements.acceptance: Fail deployment and pause; config/world/full restore executes only after scoped explicit recovery confirmation.

requirements.question: Should jobs include cron schedules, event-triggered actions, one-click maintenance presets, and dependency-aware task chains?
requirements.acceptance: Persist revision/occurrence/result for recurring/event/preset/dependency jobs; desktop reconnect never starts a second executor.

requirements.question: Can the panel ever run unattended server updates/restarts, or only outside peak hours with prior approval?
requirements.acceptance: Execute only preapproved artifact-ready maintenance while desktop is off; host downtime marks missed and ambiguous disruption is reconciled without retry.

requirements.question: Should you be able to delay a restart until no players are online and send scheduled chat broadcasts?
requirements.acceptance: Persist real five-minute countdown across disconnect, kick/save/graceful stop/start once; failed save pauses without force-kill or extra player-based approval.

requirements.question: Should backups and jobs be tied to networks/fleets or to individual servers?
requirements.acceptance: Apply fleet policy with per-server recovery history; cross-host job needing controller coordination blocks when desktop is absent.

requirements.question: Do you want a one-click disaster recovery wizard to reconstruct a host/server from a manifest and backups?
requirements.acceptance: Reconstruct a disposable host via enrollment/artifacts/config/secrets/version/health wizard; overwrite or start requires reviewed confirmation.

requirements.question: **★** Do you currently have an Apex Hosting server, or is Apex only a desired future integration?
requirements.acceptance: Keep Apex out of v1.0 completion gates even though an account exists; no working adapter is claimed.

requirements.question: If Apex: does your account visibly provide a Multicraft API key or enable API access, FTP access, and/or any other documented API?
requirements.acceptance: Leave Apex API/FTP availability unverified until adapter work; request no Apex credentials in the baseline.

requirements.question: If only unencrypted FTP exists, would you permit it after a security warning, only through a trusted tunnel, or disable it?
requirements.acceptance: Reject plaintext FTP by default; exceptional FTP requires explicit owner exception and verified encrypted tunnel.

requirements.question: Which providers should be supported after Apex: Pterodactyl, Pelican, Multicraft, Bloom, Bisect, Shockbyte, generic SFTP/SSH?
requirements.acceptance: Run separate generic SSH/SFTP, Pterodactyl, Pelican and Multicraft contracts against documented fixtures; expose only each adapter's tested features.

requirements.question: Should a hosting connector be able to manage files only, or also power, console, metrics, backups and scheduling as allowed?
requirements.acceptance: Negotiate files/power/console/metrics/backup/schedule separately; unavailable provider operation has no success-producing control.

requirements.question: Do you want an official adapter SDK with versioning, provider manifests, capability negotiation and sample connector?
requirements.acceptance: Load sample versioned manifest and run capability/scoped-credential contract kit; incompatible version or grant fails closed.

requirements.question: Should hypervisor providers (Proxmox/XCP-ng) be separate from Minecraft hosting providers and expose VM snapshots/power with confirmation?
requirements.acceptance: Inspect XCP-ng resources/snapshots/power and require VM-specific restore/power confirmation; snapshot is not called a consistent Minecraft backup.

requirements.question: Do you want Cloudflare DNS, public IP, SRV record and connection endpoint visibility/read-only checks or actual DNS editing?
requirements.acceptance: Inspect A/AAAA/SRV read-only; OpenTofu-owned records produce a reviewed workflow proposal instead of direct mutation.

requirements.question: Should health probes run from a public remote vantage point, or only from the local control plane and agents?
requirements.acceptance: Run local/agent probes with location/time; no external probe is used without enrollment and one vantage failure is not called global outage.

requirements.question: **★** Name **three desktop/web products whose design you want to emulate** (e.g., Linear, Raycast, Grafana, Proxmox, UniFi, Pterodactyl, Discord, Apple Settings) and what specifically attracts you to each.
requirements.acceptance: Review native screens for focused hierarchy/topology/staged review; reject copied Linear/UniFi/GitHub branding or proprietary assets.

requirements.question: **★** Should the aesthetic be minimalist/Apple-like, premium SaaS, developer/terminal-first, gaming-themed, glassy/futuristic, or a blend?
requirements.acceptance: Review restrained technical typography/status hierarchy and optional artwork; operational state remains legible with artwork disabled.

requirements.question: **★** Preferred accent(s) with hex codes or reference images; are Minecraft greens desired or should the interface avoid Minecraft branding colors?
requirements.acceptance: Assert light accent #2563EB and dark #60A5FA; status green/amber/red always has accompanying text/icon.

requirements.question: **★** Theme behavior: independent light and dark themes, follow OS, manual override, AMOLED black, high contrast, scheduled auto-switch?
requirements.acceptance: Follow system then persist overrides; test colorblind variants in every supported light/dark/high-contrast mode with non-color cues.

requirements.question: Base surface colors: near-black, charcoal, graphite, warm gray, cool slate, pure white, off-white, or custom?
requirements.acceptance: Inspect off-white light and graphite dark layers; navigation/content/inspector remain distinguishable without decoration.

requirements.question: Accent usage: subtle on buttons and highlights or saturated chart/status-heavy dashboard?
requirements.acceptance: Use accent on primary actions/selection/focus/chart series; neutral surfaces preserve readable operational status.

requirements.question: Layout: permanent left sidebar, collapsible rail, top navigation, command palette, split-pane workspace, or user-configurable?
requirements.acceptance: Collapse sidebar, follow breadcrumb, use global search/palette and resize context panes entirely by keyboard.

requirements.question: Content density: spacious cards, balanced pro UI, compact IDE-like tables, or density toggle?
requirements.acceptance: Switch balanced/compact layouts and persist choice; controls and form labels remain reachable without overlap.

requirements.question: Corner radius preference: square, subtle 4–6px, 8–12px, soft 16px+?
requirements.acceptance: Inspect mostly 8px radii with smaller controls/larger dialogs against tokens; extreme card rounding fails visual review.

requirements.question: Fonts: Inter, Geist, SF Pro/system, IBM Plex, JetBrains Mono for data, another?
requirements.acceptance: Disconnect network and render bundled Inter/JetBrains Mono in UI/console; font redistribution review must precede packaging.

requirements.question: Icon preference: Lucide/thin outline, filled, duotone, pixel/Minecraft hints, OS-native?
requirements.acceptance: Render consistent outline icons and tooltips/labels; unfamiliar icon-only action lacks acceptance until labeled.

requirements.question: Should light/dark palettes be symmetric or optimized independently (contrast, shadow, surface colors)?
requirements.acceptance: Test light/dark charts/borders/focus and each colorblind palette independently; a passing light palette cannot stand in for dark.

requirements.question: Do you want tasteful translucency/glass blur, gradients, grain textures, shadows, or a flat utilitarian look?
requirements.acceptance: Enable optional translucency then disable it; operational content remains opaque/readable and shadows/gradients stay restrained.

requirements.question: Animation: none, restrained 100–200ms interactions, playful microinteractions, or sophisticated transitions?
requirements.acceptance: Measure 150–200ms interaction transitions then enable reduced motion; actions are not delayed by decorative animation.

requirements.question: Should server cards show artwork/status banners, small minimalist rows, customizable widgets or multiple view modes?
requirements.acceptance: Switch default compact rows to cards/artwork; same target information and actions remain available.

requirements.question: How many metrics and actions should appear before opening a server detail page?
requirements.acceptance: Show status/players/available TPS/MSPT/memory/alerts with console and labeled action menu; absent TPS remains unavailable.

requirements.question: What should the first screen be: whole-fleet dashboard, last-opened server, network topology, favorites, or configurable?
requirements.acceptance: Cold start at fleet overview then persist favorites/last-server preference; missing last server falls back safely.

requirements.question: Should there be a persistent global console/drawer accessible from anywhere in the app?
requirements.acceptance: Drawer starts closed and opens across screens with tabs/target/connectivity; tab switch cannot send command to prior target.

requirements.question: How do you envision server grouping visually: folders, color-coded tags, expandable clusters, draggable groups, geographic sites?
requirements.acceptance: Expand networks/groups, filter tags and use favorites; colored tags retain readable names in colorblind themes.

requirements.question: Do you want an interactive topology canvas with zoom/pan, edges, proxy layers, world nodes and live traffic indicators?
requirements.acceptance: Zoom/pan graph with proxy/backend/host/status data; traffic appears only from measurements and drag never edits routes.

requirements.question: Should the staging studio be visually modeled after VS Code, GitHub Desktop, a two-pane SFTP client or a custom deployment wizard?
requirements.acceptance: Navigate files/edit/diff in three panes and add deployment basket entries; review target remains visible before approval.

requirements.question: Which chart style: simple thin-line sparklines, Grafana-like technical panels, gradient area charts, gauges, or user-selectable?
requirements.acceptance: Inspect units/tooltips/accessible series and table alternative for lines/sparklines; missing metric cannot render fabricated gauge value.

requirements.question: Alerts: prominent status rail, toast notifications, notification center, per-server badges, or all with configurable severity?
requirements.acceptance: Trigger critical condition and observe persistent banner, badge and notification history; dismissing toast cannot erase incident record.

requirements.question: Destructive actions: type server name, hold-to-confirm, two-step dialog, passkey reauthentication, or configurable by risk?
requirements.acceptance: Confirm ordinary action clearly; deletion/world overwrite requires typed target name and reviewed recovery point, wrong name blocks action.

requirements.question: Do you want dark/light app-specific logos, animated loading mark, server icons and cover images?
requirements.acceptance: Render light/dark logos/icons and optional covers locally; reduced motion suppresses animated loading decoration.

requirements.question: Should console/logs use colored Minecraft chat components, plain monospace, or switchable rendering?
requirements.acceptance: Switch safe colored/plain monospace modes and export searchable plain text; malicious formatting cannot execute links/control sequences.

requirements.question: Should custom dashboards support drag/reorder/resize/save dashboard layouts per user?
requirements.acceptance: Reorder/resize/hide/save widgets per device/user then reset; corrupt saved layout falls back to usable defaults.

requirements.question: Which screen sizes are critical (e.g., 14-inch laptop, ultrawide desktop, 1080p monitor, tablet, phone)?
requirements.acceptance: Verify native UI on 14-inch/1080p/ultrawide with scaling; add no mobile/PWA implementation to satisfy desktop layout tests.

requirements.question: Preferred native desktop UX: traditional title bar, custom chrome, tabbed windows, tray app, global keyboard shortcuts, multi-window?
requirements.acceptance: Close a window under each explicit keep-running preference with active jobs visible; native controls/tray/multi-window remain consistent.

requirements.question: Would you like a polished onboarding wizard and optional in-app guided tours/tooltips, or a no-nonsense power-user interface?
requirements.acceptance: Walk owner/enroll/adopt-or-provision/backup setup with skippable help; failure never falsely reports host adopted.

requirements.question: **★** Frontend preference: React + TypeScript, Vue, Svelte, Angular, or no preference? Vite, Next.js, TanStack Start, or another framework?
requirements.acceptance: Launch Avalonia C#/XAML MVVM app; no browser frontend substitutes for native acceptance.

requirements.question: **★** Backend preference: C#/.NET, Node/TypeScript (Nest/Fastify), Go, Rust, or another? Do you want the host agent in the same language?
requirements.acceptance: Invoke local .NET 10 services from UI with separate domain/persistence/jobs/transport layers; no hosted web administration dependency exists.

requirements.question: **★** Desktop preference: Tauri 2, Electron, Avalonia/.NET, Qt, Flutter, or compare before deciding?
requirements.acceptance: Keep management core alive independently of windows per preference; no Tauri/Rust sidecar replaces Avalonia.

requirements.question: **★** Mobile preference: responsive web/PWA only, native iOS+Android via Expo/React Native, Tauri mobile, Flutter, or later milestone?
requirements.acceptance: Scope review and package inventory contain no mobile app, responsive administration UI or PWA deliverable.

requirements.question: For a React UI: Tailwind/shadcn+Radix, Material UI, Mantine, Fluent UI, custom primitives, or another?
requirements.acceptance: Use native Avalonia templates/tokens; keyboard/focus/labels work in independent high-contrast and colorblind palettes.

requirements.question: For .NET backend: EF Core, Dapper/raw SQL, or mixed; Minimal APIs vs controllers; OpenAPI client generation style?
requirements.acceptance: Call services directly and persist EF Core/SQLite versioned data; telemetry raw SQL needs measured justification and parameterization.

requirements.question: Should telemetry/console use WebSockets, Server-Sent Events, gRPC streams (agent), or let architecture team decide?
requirements.acceptance: Stream agent events over versioned outbound gRPC/mTLS and local UI observables; reconnect refreshes state/results without replaying mutations.

requirements.question: Should host agents use C#/.NET, Go (single static binary), Rust, Java, or align with backend?
requirements.acceptance: Run self-contained C# agent under restricted systemd account with separate helper; approved local jobs persist across desktop loss.

requirements.question: Should JVM bridge plugins be Java or Kotlin? Which JDK and build tools (Gradle/Maven)?
requirements.acceptance: Build each Java bridge via pinned Gradle/JDK/bytecode target per family; reject a host-Java-25-only compatibility assumption.

requirements.question: **★** SQLite is fixed: do you prefer EF Core migrations, raw SQL + FluentMigrator, or another explicit migration mechanism?
requirements.acceptance: Lock and back up local SQLite before migration; interruption/newer schema blocks unsafe access and restore uses compatible backup, never blind downgrade.

requirements.question: Monorepo orchestration preference: pnpm + Turborepo, Nx, Bun, yarn workspaces, custom `just` commands, or no preference?
requirements.acceptance: Build native solution projects and separate in-repo Gradle bridge project; no web monorepo tooling requirement is introduced.

requirements.question: Dependency and build tooling: pinned versions via mise/asdf/Volta, `global.json`, Gradle wrapper, dev containers, Nix, or normal local installs?
requirements.acceptance: Reproduce restore with pinned SDK, centralized NuGet and locks plus Gradle wrapper/JDK pins; unreviewed version drift fails checks.

requirements.question: API style: REST+OpenAPI, GraphQL, gRPC, or hybrid with streaming transports?
requirements.acceptance: Use direct local interfaces and versioned mTLS gRPC; use authenticated IPC only where processes require it.

requirements.question: Should plugin/provider integrations be dynamically loadable runtime plugins, compile-time modules, or versioned external processes?
requirements.acceptance: Compile built-in adapters normally and isolate executable extensions by grants/process; privileged helper refuses extension loading.

requirements.question: Docker/Compose local development required? Linux development environment with actual systemd test VM available?
requirements.acceptance: Run native builds without Docker and destructive integration in disposable Debian 13 VM; no production worlds are used as resettable fixtures.

requirements.question: Native desktop packaging: DMG/PKG, signed `.app`, Windows MSIX/MSI/EXE, Linux AppImage/DEB/RPM/Flatpak—what must ship first?
requirements.acceptance: Install/upgrade Windows x64 and macOS Intel/ARM .app DMG on chosen minimum OS versions; untested minimums remain unclaimed.

requirements.question: Are you able/willing to sign macOS/Windows releases and use Apple/Windows developer accounts? Unsigned dev builds okay initially?
requirements.acceptance: Label unsigned dev builds; block stable installer publication without Windows signing and macOS signing/notarization evidence and separate credentials.

requirements.question: Update mechanism: GitHub Releases with user-approved updates, auto-update service, manual installers only, or custom host?
requirements.acceptance: Show GitHub release notes/authenticity and require install approval; active-job conflict blocks unsafe update and failed update offers recovery.

requirements.question: Backend deployment packaging: standalone binary, Docker image, systemd service, Debian package, Kubernetes Helm chart, all or prioritized?
requirements.acceptance: Install self-contained Debian agent through reviewed SSH installer; agent identity cannot replace privileged helper during update.

requirements.question: Where should user settings/secrets live: OS keychain, control plane secret store, optional external Vault, or both with explicit ownership?
requirements.acceptance: Store secret values in Windows protected storage/macOS Keychain and references in SQLite; ordinary export/log contains no secret and revocation works.

requirements.question: Should the desktop app function offline for read-only cached data/staging edits, or require backend connection?
requirements.acceptance: Disconnect agent and inspect cached stale state/edit staging/draft; new remote execution disabled while approved agent-local jobs continue.

requirements.question: **★** Who will access the panel: just you on a LAN, VPN users, trusted friends, moderators, or internet-wide public administration?
requirements.acceptance: Initialize sole local owner with LAN/VPN host access; no internet-wide admin login is enabled.

requirements.question: **★** Should login be local accounts, OS-auth desktop unlock, GitHub/Google OAuth, passkeys, TOTP, SSO/OIDC, or combinations?
requirements.acceptance: Bind owner to OS user and test OS reauthentication where supported/optional passphrase; no mandatory online account is requested.

requirements.question: Is multi-user RBAC required now? If yes, which roles and exact allowed actions (viewer, moderator, operator, deployer, owner)?
requirements.acceptance: Invoke core mutations without valid owner permission and deny; single-owner UI cannot bypass future scoped permission boundaries.

requirements.question: Do you want per-host and per-server permissions, not just global roles?
requirements.acceptance: Request service/file/integration access to a different target and deny on core/agent/helper despite valid identity elsewhere.

requirements.question: Should destructive deploy/restore actions require a second approval or an MFA step?
requirements.acceptance: Require owner reauthentication, target-name and recovery review for destructive restore/deletion; no second-person requirement is introduced.

requirements.question: Is outbound-only agent connectivity important so that no inbound firewall holes are required on VMs?
requirements.acceptance: Capture agent connection initiation outbound to desktop; expose no required inbound host-management listener.

requirements.question: Are you willing to run a private CA/certificate provisioning system for mTLS, or prefer enrollment tokens + HTTPS and rotation?
requirements.acceptance: Enroll with single-use token and per-agent cert; test rotation/revocation and scope CA to app rather than global OS trust.

requirements.question: What is your trusted network model: LAN-only, WireGuard/Tailscale-only, Cloudflare Access tunnel, exposed HTTPS with authentication?
requirements.acceptance: Bind/restrict listener to approved LAN/VPN; public exposure or firewall edits require explicit owner approval.

requirements.question: Should session/audit logs be immutable/exportable and how long should they be retained?
requirements.acceptance: Append redacted exportable events with default 365-day retention and tamper detection; document OS attacker can rewrite SQLite history.

requirements.question: Should the UI offer emergency read-only mode or lock deploys/restarts during incidents?
requirements.acceptance: Enable read-only incident mode and block new mutations while showing active jobs/safe cancel; unlock requires owner confirmation.

requirements.question: Should secrets be centrally shared among servers or isolated per integration/server with explicit scope and rotation?
requirements.acceptance: Rotate/revoke a per-server integration credential; unrelated scopes remain isolated and explicit sharing is visible.

requirements.question: Is there any need for guest/public read-only server status pages separate from the private admin panel?
requirements.acceptance: Provide sanitized status export without built-in public website or private operational/credential fields.

requirements.question: **★** How many implementation agents may run concurrently (2, 3, 5, more), considering API quota and cost?
requirements.acceptance: Lead records at most four concurrent roles with explicit limits; this implementation child spawns none.

requirements.question: **★** Which should be lead orchestrator—Claude or Codex—and which specific *currently available* model/reasoning level do you prefer?
requirements.acceptance: Record approved GPT-6.1 Sol high availability at kickoff; unavailable model blocks substitution until owner approves.

requirements.question: Which agents are preferred for backend, frontend, UI design, JVM plugins, integrations, and security, and should the orchestrator select dynamically?
requirements.acceptance: Assign focused role/ownership/acceptance to each bounded task; reject unapproved provider/model substitution.

requirements.question: **★** Three QA agents as functional, security/reliability and UX/accessibility/performance: good, or would you change their specializations?
requirements.acceptance: Assign independent functional, security and UX/performance verdicts by risk; implementation author cannot approve own work.

requirements.question: Are you happy requiring three independent QA verdicts on high-risk PRs and two including security on regular PRs?
requirements.acceptance: Require two regular or three high-risk independent QA verdicts and a verified identity/check mechanism; same-account personas never count as distinct GitHub approvals.

requirements.question: Should the boss merge eligible PRs automatically, or request your approval for every PR/major milestone?
requirements.acceptance: Lead merges only eligible reviewed PR; scope/architecture/license/expanded privilege/public release changes require owner approval.

requirements.question: Should workers create GitHub Issues and PRs directly, or only have lead agent do GitHub mutations?
requirements.acceptance: Worker opens assigned PR while lead owns issue planning/merges; QA returns evidence instead of merging own reviewed change.

requirements.question: Do you want one issue per feature slice, one PR per issue, or more granular subfeature PRs?
requirements.acceptance: Map bounded issue to reviewable PR with dependencies; oversized slices split without dropping source IDs.

requirements.question: Branch naming: `feat/*`, `fix/*`, `agent/*`, issue-number prefixes, or another convention?
requirements.acceptance: Use docs/1-requirements-baseline for issue 1 and issue-number prefixed delivery branches for later slices.

requirements.question: GitHub Actions CI only, or add local Git hooks, pre-commit, Buildkite, self-hosted runners?
requirements.acceptance: Run local checks and isolated GitHub Actions; untrusted PR receives no production or signing credentials.

requirements.question: Should branch protection demand signed commits, CODEOWNERS, merge queue, mandatory status checks and history linearity?
requirements.acceptance: Verify signed commits/linear history/CODEOWNERS/checks/protection and merge queue availability; do not claim enforcement without repository evidence.

requirements.question: Do you want release builds for macOS/Windows/Linux on every PR, nightly, weekly, or tagged releases only?
requirements.acceptance: Build/test Windows/macOS/Linux-agent targets per PR and stable installers only from approved tags; unexecuted runner tests remain pending.

requirements.question: Preferred test frameworks by language (xUnit/NUnit/MSTest, Vitest/Jest, Playwright/Cypress, JUnit5/Kotest)?
requirements.acceptance: Execute xUnit/Avalonia headless plus native Windows/macOS, JUnit bridges, provider contracts and disposable Debian cases at dependent slices; mocks do not certify systemd.

requirements.question: What minimum critical-code coverage and mutation-testing targets do you expect; accept initial defaults of >=90% line, >=85% branch, >=80% mutation for safety modules?
requirements.acceptance: Publish safety-module reports meeting 90% line/85% branch/80% applicable mutation; fail gate on regression or meaningless skipped assertions.

requirements.question: Should QA include accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA), visual screenshots, chaos testing, fuzzing, provider contract tests and cross-platform installers?
requirements.acceptance: Collect keyboard/screen-reader/contrast/colorblind/motion/visual/installer/fuzz/provider/chaos evidence; interrupted backup/partition/full disk/partial deployment recover truthfully.

requirements.question: Which external coding tools may agents use: GitHub CLI, Codex MCP, Claude SDK, container runtime, SSH to test VMs, browser automation, Figma?
requirements.acceptance: Use approved local/GitHub/.NET/Gradle/MCP/native-test tools; additional paid service or credential use requires owner approval.

requirements.question: Should agents enforce zero `TODO` placeholders in shipped critical paths, complete API documentation, SBOM, SAST, license checks and secret scans?
requirements.acceptance: Scan dependencies/licenses/secrets/SAST/SBOM and critical paths; placeholder success or unsupported-as-working behavior fails release gate.

requirements.question: How often should lead agent report progress: after each merged PR, after every milestone, on failures only, or scheduled summaries?
requirements.acceptance: Report actual checks/commits/next work during active work and after merges/milestones; surface blocker immediately without claiming unrun tests pass.

requirements.question: **★** Can agents modify **sandbox/test** VMs automatically, and which actions must always require authorization on the real live server?
requirements.acceptance: Use protected recorded necessary production actions only under lead scope and verified backups; this docs task contacts no production host and never resets worlds.

requirements.question: Should the app expose an assistant that reads logs and suggests fixes, or may also draft staged changes (never autoapply)?
requirements.acceptance: Local assistant explains sanitized logs and drafts staged changes only; external AI needs opt-in/disclosed data and no assistant executes changes.

requirements.question: Do you want optional GitOps: deploy when a GitHub branch/tag changes, after review and preflight?
requirements.acceptance: Import approved branch/tag into deployment draft; repository update never directly mutates a server.

requirements.question: Should the app offer plugin compatibility testing against an isolated duplicate Minecraft server before production promotion?
requirements.acceptance: Run plugin compatibility on disposable native duplicate with separate files/ports/limits and external integrations disabled; production worlds are never mounted as working files.

requirements.question: Would you like dynamic resource suggestions (e.g. JVM heap, chunk distance, GC) backed by telemetry with human approval?
requirements.acceptance: Suggest resource adjustment with telemetry evidence and restart impact; approval/staging required before any change.

requirements.question: Should users be able to configure Discord notifications, community status pages, public dashboards or a bot for basic server controls?
requirements.acceptance: Opt-in Discord and sanitized status exports work; no bot controls or built-in public dashboard is enabled.

requirements.question: Should the server network have a built-in player-facing maintenance page, MOTD configuration, icon, custom domains and SRV record checks?
requirements.acceptance: Review MOTD/icon/maintenance messages/endpoints/SRV diagnostics respecting DNS ownership; no browser maintenance page is added.

requirements.question: Do you want automatic blue/green server replacement, rolling migrations or traffic draining across compatible proxy backends?
requirements.acceptance: Review/drain compatible replacement backend and handle world-state explicitly; unsupported blue/green is blocked without claiming zero downtime.

requirements.question: Should managing custom mods/modpacks via Modrinth/CurseForge be part of the MVP or postponed?
requirements.acceptance: Stage manual/Modrinth/selected documented catalog modpack with loader/MC/Java/dependency/license checks; incompatible or nonredistributable content is flagged/blocked as appropriate.

requirements.question: Should the app support a third-party extension marketplace later (theme, provider adapter, Minecraft plugin integration, dashboard widget)?
requirements.acceptance: Install curated or manual offline manifest with compatibility/grant review; no marketplace account is required and revoked extension loses access.

requirements.question: Finally: **describe your ideal three-minute demo**. What exact clicks, screens, animations, actions and results would make you say, “This is precisely the panel I wanted”?
requirements.acceptance: Demonstrate native overview/live metrics/stage/diff/recovery approval/job history; keep real five-minute countdown and use prior completion for three-minute walkthrough.

owner_overrides.provenance: Later explicit owner message in issue-1 implementation session, 2026-11-13
owner_overrides.policy: No C# var anywhere; explicit types in production, tests and checked-in generated code.
